summary: A zod-checked DeviceProfile (pacing budgets, render budget and limits, three render switches) in four bundled JSONs under config/profiles, resolved in main (userData override, STAR_CHART_PROFILE pin, fallback with notice), passed to the renderer via a launch argument, and fed to the schedule as budgets; recommend three builds.

split.title: The profile: schema, bundles, resolver, loader, env, Settings display, docs
Pacing budgets through the profile; remove BUDGET_MS and HIGHLIGHT_BUDGET_MS; scripts' EngineInputs
Render switches, effect cap, frame budget in perf.spec, test hooks, phone e2e

notes: About 35 files in all, so the split; each part is 10-15 files and leaves the tree green. C4b and C4c both touch testHooks.ts and 15 §10, so run them in sequence, not in parallel.

Decided: only the two code-constant budgets go in pacing; gap shape stays in constants.ts. Label caps and a holo-filter switch are left out (planner/projection feed the goldens; B1 showed filters are not Pulsar's cost). Switch set is paint, twinkle, ornament plus maxActiveFx; C3 adds keys beside them.
Profile reaches the renderer by a launch argument, not IPC, so the first schedule has the right budget; overrides apply at next launch.
Real schedules run well over budget (Comet 67 s against 45 s), so the phone e2e asserts fewer/shorter beats than desktop, not totalMs <= budget; the builder confirms which comparison holds on Pulsar.
Profile values for laptop-battery, tablet and phone are starting guesses, to be tuned on devices.
scripts/pacing-candidates.ts was written by C2 (now committed); C4b changes one line there and must keep the committed pacing-ledger.md output unchanged without --profile.
